figures.caption: Figure 1: Left: Time-lagged dynamic connectivity matrix representing directed interaction dynamics. Middle: Conventional directed-network analysis represents pairwise interactions on a graph. Right: The proposed framework represents interactions on a simplicial complex encoding nodes, edges, and faces. The topology does not impose cyclic organization a priori; persistent cyclic structure is inferred from the observed interaction flow through variational dynamics on this scaffold.

Figure 2: The gradient and curl flows XG and XC correspond to dissipative structures of the original flow X that decay under Dirichlet–Hodge diffusion. In contrast, the harmonic flow XH is non-dissipative and therefore persists under diffusion, encoding the globally consistent, topologically constrained circulation that remains after transient components dissipate.

Figure 3: Two networks contain partially inconsistent cyclic structure involving 2 → 4 → 5. Direct algebraic averaging removes this cycle and instead introduces a spurious cycle 2 → 4 → 3 that is not present in either network. In contrast, averaging in the harmonic cycle space enhances the coherent recurrent cycle 5 → 2 → 4 → 5.

Figure 8: Top 10 cycles out of 534 identified from the mean harmonic flow Ū across 400 human brain networks (p < 10−29). The cycles repeatedly involve shared brain regions but not identical directed edges, indicating reproducible cyclic organization at the node level rather than exact edgewise recurrence. This explains why direct edgeweight averaging fails to align cycles.
